# Operations

- OPS-007: An ASP.NET Core app follows Microsoft's ASP.NET Core best practices: avoid blocking calls; make hot code paths asynchronous and call data access, I/O and long-running operations asynchronously where an asynchronous API exists; avoid reading large request bodies or response bodies into memory; never create and dispose HttpClient instances directly, and use HttpClientFactory to retrieve them (OPS-008 names the lifetime options); do not use HttpContext after the request is complete, and do not access it from multiple threads. For high-performance logging, use LoggerMessageAttribute with compile-time source generation.
- OPS-008: Use either long-lived HttpClient instances with SocketsHttpHandler.PooledConnectionLifetime set, or short-lived clients created by IHttpClientFactory; what matters is that clients aren't created and disposed with each request. If an app requires cookies, avoid IHttpClientFactory, whose pooled handlers share CookieContainer objects. Add only one resilience handler to a client and avoid stacking handlers.
- OPS-011: Every log call in an app goes through a generated, LoggerMessage-based method, not a logger extension method such as LogInformation.
